characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Optical microscope (OM, NOVEL, MR5000) at 200 × magnification
characterization_methods.key_findings: M1-30 exhibits equiaxed grain morphology similar to M1-SS; grain size shows no significant change after aging, maintaining an average of 45.3 ± 9.3 μm.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Metallographic samples extracted parallel to the rolled surface; ground with SiC papers and polished with 1.5 μm diamond suspension; etched with 3 % FeCl3 + 10 % HCl (in ethanol) for 10–20 s; grain size measured per GB/T 6394-2002.
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize phase morphology and measure grain size of M1-30.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: TEM, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Talos F200X G2
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fig. 4(a–c) BF, DF and SAED show a large number of κ-carbides with number density around 7 × 10^22 m^-3 uniformly distributed in the Ti/V-free M1 steel; SAED (ZA=[0 1̄ 1]) shows matrix reflections (111), (200), (111) and extra κ reflections.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: TEM samples mechanically ground to 50 μm, 3 mm discs punched and thinned with a Gatan precision ion polishing system; BF/DF images with 100 nm scale bars and SAED patterns with 2 1/nm scale bars.
characterization_methods.purpose: Investigate morphology, crystal structure, chemical composition and dislocation configuration of the κ-carbides in M1-30.
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM): bright-field (BF) and dark-field (DF) imaging and selected area electron diffraction (SAED)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: TEM, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Talos F200X G2
characterization_methods.key_findings: Deformation mode of M1 is the plane (planar) slip of dislocations; dense dark dislocation tangles/cell walls and slip bands are observed; slip-band spacing of M2 is significantly smaller than that of M1.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Post-tensile gauge region; TEM BF images with 200 nm scale bars.
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the deformation mode (slip behavior) of M1-30 after tensile testing.
characterization_methods.technique: TEM of the uniformly deformed region after tensile testing

characterization_methods.key_findings: M1-30 yield strength 860 MPa with elongation reduced to ~40 %; work-hardening rate significantly reduced compared with M1-SS.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 2 mm thick, 58 mm long specimens along the rolling direction; strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; room temperature; 12.5 mm extensometer; yield strength at 0.2 % offset.
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the mechanical properties (yield strength, elongation, work-hardening rate) of M1-30.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: M1 steel composition after aging treatment at 550 °C for 30 h.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Consistent with TEM observations that the matrix remains single-phase austenite after aging.

analytical_models.model_note: Ti and V elements have little influence on the SFE; M2 SFE is ~78 mJ/m^2. The high SFE indicates the deformation mode is dislocation slip.

parameters.name: ρ (molar surface density on {111} planes, M1)

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Composition of M1; ρ = 2.8 × 10^-5 mol/m^2 for M1; σ^{γ/ε} = 10 mJ/m^2 interfacial energy; grain-size effect term ~1–2 mJ/m^2.
computational_details.simulation_method: Stacking fault energy calculation using the Olson–Cohen thermodynamic model
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Consistent with TEM observation that the deformation mode of M1 is dislocation slip.

analytical_models.model_note: Both M1 and M2 underwent high-temperature solution treatment so dislocation strengthening can be essentially neglected.

parameters.name: σ0 (matrix strength: lattice friction + solution strengthening)
D (average austenite grain size of M1-30)

analytical_models.model_note: Because the critical size of κ-carbides is greater than 20 nm, the shearing mechanism is adopted; chemical and stacking-fault strengthening have little impact. Coherency strengthening (eq. 3), modulus-mismatch strengthening (eq. 4) and order strengthening (eq. 5).

parameters.name: ΔG (modulus misfit between austenite and κ-carbides)

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: M1-30: single-phase austenite matrix with uniformly precipitated κ-carbides (r = 10.8 nm, f = 7.4 %); no (Ti, V)C carbides.
computational_details.simulation_method: Quantitative yield-strength contribution calculation based on strengthening mechanisms
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated mechanism contributions sum to the measured yield strength in Fig. 10; the increase in yield strength of M1 after aging is mainly due to shear strengthening of κ-carbides.

analytical_models.model_note: Used to extract the work-hardening index n of M1-30 (Fig. 11a).

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: True stress–true strain data of M1-30 tensile test.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Work-hardening of aged M1 divided into two stages (Stage I rapid slip, Stage II planar slip), consistent with reduced work-hardening rate observed in tensile curves (Fig. 7).

defect_interactions.interaction_type: planar dislocation slip with shearing of coherent κ-carbides (glide plane softening)
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: The deformation mode of M1 is planar slip of dislocations; the highly coherent κ-carbides are cut (sheared) by dislocations, destroying the coherency relationship and softening the glide plane, which reduces the work-hardening rate of M1-30. The homogeneous precipitation of κ-carbides prevents refinement of the slip band and reduces the work-hardening index of M1 after aging.

interfaces.interface_notes: In M1-30 no (Ti, V)C carbides are present (the table shows '-' for M1-30); κ-carbides are the only intragranular precipitate and are highly coherent with the matrix.
interfaces.phase_evolution: Supersaturated austenite matrix decomposes into solute-depleted and solute-enriched regions; when sufficient driving force is attained the solute-enriched regions transform into L-ordered domains and carbon ordering forms κ-carbides (generally attributed to spinodal decomposition). In the Ti/V-free M1 matrix with homogeneous chemical composition, κ-carbides exhibit a uniform distribution.

phase_interfaces.coherence: high coherence (κ-carbides show much higher coherence with the matrix than (Ti, V)C carbides)

interfaces.slip_behavior: Planar dislocation slip (SFE ~70 mJ/m^2); the slip-band spacing of M2 is significantly smaller than that of M1, but both steels deform by planar slip.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Ultimate tensile strength: Ti/V-free M1-30 = 1004 MPa vs Ti/V-modified M2-30 = 1096 MPa; yield strength comparable (M1-30 860 MPa vs M2-30 884 MPa); M1-30 shows a significant reduction in work-hardening rate after aging whereas M2-30 maintains its work-hardening capacity.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The material was melted in a high-vacuum electric-arc melting furnace.

processing_steps.method: hot rolling followed by water quenching
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The ingots were hot rolled from 20 to 2 mm at 1000 °C followed by water quenching.
The samples were solution-processed at 1000 °C for 30 min and water quenched; this state is named M1-SS and is the parent process of the aging treatment.
Aging at 550 °C for 30 h followed by water quenching; the resulting aged M1 steel is named M1-30.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Yield strength determined at a 0.2 % offset; specimens ground with silicon carbide abrasive papers to remove surface scratches.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: 2 mm thick, 58 mm long tensile specimens fabricated along the rolling direction; 12.5 mm extensometer to measure gauge-length deformation

strain_hardening_rate.value: Significant reduction in work-hardening rate after aging (solid black vs dashed lines); the aged M1 work hardening is divided into two stages (Stage I rapid slip of dislocations, Stage II planar slip of dislocations), whereas solution-treated M1 shows three stages.

precipitates.coherency: highly coherent with the austenite matrix
precipitates.distribution: uniformly distributed within the matrix (intragranular); number density of around 7 × 10^22 m^-3

structures.overall_structure: Equiaxed austenite grains containing straight annealing twins; the matrix remains single-phase austenite after 30 h aging at 550 °C (thermodynamic calculations confirm single-phase austenite after aging), and contains a large number of fine κ-carbides uniformly distributed within the grain interior.

unmapped_findings: The stacking fault energy (SFE) of M1 was calculated as approximately 70 mJ/m^2 (M2 ~78 mJ/m^2), indicating that the deformation mode of the material is dislocation slip; Ti and V have little influence on the SFE.
The number density of κ-carbides in M1-30 is around 7 × 10^22 m^-3.

The κ-carbide shearing strengthening in M1-30 is unchanged in nature from that of κ-carbides that precipitate uniformly; the yield strength increase of M1 after aging is mainly due to shear strengthening of the κ-carbides.

In M1-30 there are no (Ti, V)C carbides (Table 3 reports '-' for M1 for both solution-treated and 30 h aged conditions); only κ-carbides are present with volume fraction 7.4 ± 3.4 % and mean radius 10.8 ± 6.2 nm.
Adding Ti and V does not alter the austenitic phase composition of the low-density steel but refines the grain size (M1 42.4 ± 7.8 μm → M2 32.3 ± 10.4 μm in the solution-treated state).
